chapter: Bix's methods and New Orleans musicians
title: Nick LaRocca and the old New Orleans musicians
summary: Hug recalls writing tunes with LaRocca and praises the old musicians' generosity.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Oh, wonderful people. You just can't imagine. Wonderful people. And his wife, you know? His wife. You meet these guys, you know? And they didn't call her mama for that. She took care of everybody.
Sure. And Nick LaRocca. Nick LaRocca's another person that very few people got to know real well. Because he was sort of a little bit cantankerous and a little bit obnoxious, you know?
He tried to claim everybody. Yeah.

It started with him just like Jolly Roll. But if you got to know him, I mean, you know, and if he liked you. I mean, he was a funny, he was a real funny old guy. I mean, I worked with him right towards the end. When he died, I worked right up to the time that he died. I wrote about, I guess maybe, 15, 20 tunes with him. And he was wonderful to know him. I mean, the funny things that he told me, you know? Because all the Walden's musicians had funny stories.
You know, we got about eight and a half hours of Nick on tape. Did I ever tell you that? More than that.
Eight and a half hours that I did.
You know, that's other stuff. That should be good. I'd like to hear that sometimes.
Well, you never have the time. You're so busy.

Yeah, Nick was something else, believe me. He said, they don't believe I wrote Tiger, right? Come here, I'll show you. He goes to the drawer, address the drawer, and he pulls the copyright out of the drawer, you see? Well, of course, you can't deny the fact that he had the copyright, but they say so many people had it. So many people played it before, you know, and all that sort of thing. Of course, tunes, that's something else. Everybody says somebody stole something from him, you know?

That's been going on since the beginning of time. But the musicians themselves and the kind of music they played, well, that is the thing we're mostly interested in here right now. And I can only say one thing. I don't think that anywhere, there can be anywhere in the world that there were musicians like Noel as musicians. I'm not speaking as the picture of today. I don't think it's the same, do you think?
No, I think there are less musicians coming up.

I don't think it's nearly the same now with the ones, the old timers dying off, you know. But the old timers, I mean, there was just something about those musicians. I mean, I don't know. Even though they may have been terrible, they may have hated you. But when you were around them, if they thought you needed them, they'd be the first ones to help you, you know? It was that kind of a thing. And this is what was so great about them. I mean, you'd see, even Tishockey, he would talk about musicians, but you'd turn around and he'd help somebody, you know? And Julian Lane and, of course, even amongst the white musicians, even amongst the black musicians, too. It was that way, too, you know? The competition, the competitive thing was always great in the audience, you know? And, of course, this is what caused a little feeling of animosity on some of their parts, you know, which I guess you can understand to a great extent. That exists in almost anything. Well, there's a keen spirit of competition. There's bound to be animosity. But probably this is what made it so great. It was that everybody thought that they were the ones and they were the best. And they would be the first ones to tell you so. Jell-Erold was an example. Jell-Erold, Nick LaRocca, and some of the others, they'd be the first ones to tell you that they were the greatest. And that's what really made it interesting.

Bill Crayton and we used to figure out, and we can talk about this after the tapes over, an all-star band where you'd get together. Everybody created jazz and the whole mix of that, each one, you know? They would have made a good band, except they'd have hated each other.
